issues.sym: The engine revs up without the vehicle speeding up, shifts feel rough or strange, the overdrive (O/D) light blinks, or the transmission stops pulling altogether.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic in these years wears out internally, often with burnt fluid, and failures from about 50,000 to 130,000 miles are the top Mariner complaint. Owners report full rebuilds, some more than once.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell. If the O/D light blinks or it slips, have it diagnosed right away; stop driving hard, because slipping quickly makes the damage worse.

issues.t: Transmission stops working or goes into limp mode
issues.sym: The transmission slips, will not shift, drops into a reduced-power limp mode, or stops moving the vehicle.
issues.why: Owners of 2009-2011 Mariners, including the hybrid, report transmission failures, usually from about 60,000 to 110,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked as soon as shifting changes. Ask a dealer about software updates for your VIN before agreeing to a replacement.

issues.t: Electric power steering assist cuts out (recall)
issues.sym: A power steering warning appears and the steering suddenly becomes very heavy, often while turning at low speed.
issues.why: A torque sensor in the electric power steering can stop reading the driver's input and shut off the assist. Ford recalled 2008-2011 Mariners built from August 2006 to September 2010, and steering failures are the most-reported Mariner problem.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V-284. If the assist drops out, grip the wheel firmly, slow down and pull over. Have it fixed before regular driving.

issues.t: Throttle body failure cuts engine power
issues.sym: A wrench light or a message to pull over, then the engine loses power or stalls, sometimes at highway speed. It may run normally after a restart and then do it again.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body's motor and sensor wear out, so the engine computer can no longer trust it and cuts power. Owners most often fix it with a new throttle body.
issues.next: Have the throttle body tested and replaced; losing power in traffic is dangerous. Ask a dealer whether any Ford extended coverage applies to your VIN.

issues.sym: Hybrid warning lights, a check engine light, reduced power, or the hybrid system shutting down while driving.
issues.why: The electric pump that cools the hybrid electronics can fail, letting them overheat and shut down the powertrain. Ford recalled 2006-2008 Mariner Hybrids.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V-526. If hybrid warnings come on and power drops, pull over safely.

issues.t: Fuel pump module can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell, especially after filling up, or fuel wetness near the rear of the vehicle.
issues.why: The fuel delivery module on top of the tank could crack and leak fuel. Ford recalled 3.0L V6 Mariners built from February 2009 to December 2010.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-777. Avoid topping off the tank and have any fuel smell checked right away.

issues.t: Shift lever can disconnect from the transmission (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter feels loose, or the vehicle is not in the gear the shifter shows; it may roll when the shifter says Park.
issues.why: A bolt connecting the shift lever to the transmission could come loose. RepairPal lists this recall for four Mariner model years.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and check your VIN for the shift lever recall.

issues.sym: The wipers slow down, grind, or stop in rain or snow.
issues.why: The wiper motor gear could be built without grease, wear out and break. Ford recalled affected vehicles.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 05V-520 before bad-weather driving.

issues.t: Rear window glass shatters without warning
issues.sym: The rear liftgate glass suddenly breaks, parked or while driving, leaving glass inside the cargo area.
issues.why: Owners report the flip-up rear glass shattering on its own. The cause is not confirmed; stress at the glass hinges or a defroster fault are suspected.
issues.next: Clean up carefully and cover the opening. Replacement glass is usually a quick job for a glass shop; check whether your insurance covers glass.

issues.t: Liftgate glass breaks on its own
issues.sym: The rear liftgate window shatters with no impact, even on a nearly new vehicle.
issues.why: Owners of 2011 Mariners also report the rear glass exploding without warning. The cause is not confirmed.
issues.next: Cover the opening and have the glass replaced. Ask the dealer to inspect the glass hinges and struts at the same time.

issues.t: Engine stalls or loses power while driving
issues.sym: The engine sputters or cuts out at speed, the check engine light comes on, and it may not restart.
issues.why: Owners of early Mariners report stalling from causes including a failed idle air control valve, a bad ignition coil and leaking intake gaskets on the V6, and in some cases serious engine damage.
issues.next: Pull over safely and have the codes read before driving further. If the oil light came on or the engine knocks, do not restart it; have it towed.

issues.t: Knock or pop from the steering column when turning
issues.sym: A knock, pop or clunk felt in the steering wheel when turning, especially at low speed or when parking.
issues.why: Looseness in the steering shaft or its U-joint coupling. RepairPal lists this as the most common Mariner problem.
issues.next: Have the steering shaft and coupling checked. It is usually a noise problem, but any looseness in the steering should be repaired.

issues.t: Hybrid brake system warning and brake failure
issues.sym: ABS, brake and 'regen brakes disabled' warnings, a 'service brake system' message, dragging brakes, or the brakes failing to stop the vehicle as expected.
issues.why: The hybrid uses an electronically controlled brake system that blends regenerative and friction braking. Owners report failures of its hydraulic control unit, which are costly to fix.
issues.next: Do not drive with brake warnings on. Have the brake system diagnosed by a dealer or hybrid specialist right away.

issues.t: Brake pedal sinks or brakes fade from ABS unit fault
issues.sym: The brake pedal travels much farther than usual, or about half of the braking seems to disappear.
issues.why: Owners report valves in the ABS unit sticking and letting brake fluid bypass part of the system. One fix reported was a new ABS modulator.
issues.next: Stop driving and have the brakes inspected. Ask a dealer to check for any open brake recalls on your VIN.

issues.t: Rust in rear wheel wells and quarter panels
issues.sym: Blistering paint and rust around the rear wheel openings and lower rear doors.
issues.why: Owners report rust starting around the rear wheel wells at about 80,000-90,000 miles.
issues.next: Have rust treated early while it is still on the surface. Rinse salt from the wheel wells in winter.

issues.t: Water leaks into the cabin or cargo area
issues.sym: Wet carpet in the footwell or cargo area after rain.
issues.why: Owners report water getting into the cabin, with door seals, body seams or blocked drains as typical sources.
issues.next: Have a body shop or dealer water-test the vehicle to find the entry point, and dry the carpet quickly to prevent mold.

issues.t: Blower motor cuts out or HVAC actuator clicks
issues.sym: The heater fan turns off and on by itself, or a clicking or ticking from behind the dash when adjusting the heat.
issues.why: Owners report intermittent blower motors and noisy heater door actuators.
issues.next: Have the blower motor, its resistor and the actuator checked. These are usually inexpensive repairs.

issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only slightly cool air, or works only some of the time.
issues.why: Owners of 2009 and 2010 Mariners report A/C systems that stop cooling properly. Refrigerant leaks and compressor or clutch faults are the usual causes.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested and the compressor checked before paying for a recharge.
